headline: Wet, windy Thanksgiving, coastal flooding risk through Friday, and more rain early next week.
summary: A run of Pacific storms keeps the pattern active through the end of the week. A warm front lifts north today, a cold front follows Thursday, and a weaker system arrives Friday, moving over high pressure building toward California. Forecasters expect a brief lull over the weekend, but they are less certain about it, and another round of systems is likely early next week. For Thanksgiving, expect a wet, windy day, with strong gusts on the coast and in the northern interior and breezy conditions around Puget Sound. Rain totals range from about an inch in the lowlands to several inches in the Olympics and Cascades. Winds ease Thursday afternoon, but coastal flooding remains the bigger worry through Friday.
